title: Classic Bread Sauce with Clove-Studded Onion
summary: A gentle, creamy sauce made by infusing milk with onion and clove before thickening it with breadcrumbs and butter.
equipment: warm serving bowl or sauce boat

ingredients.item: whole milk, plus extra if needed
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Stud
steps.text: Stud the onion with the cloves and tie the bay leaf, thyme and parsley stalks together with string.

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Put the onion, herbs, 480 ml milk, salt and pepper in a saucepan, bring to just below a simmer, then keep on the lowest heat for 20 min without boiling.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Lift out the onion and herbs.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Stir in 60 g breadcrumbs and the nutmeg and cook on very low, stirring, until thick and creamy, 5-8 min, loosening with a little milk or adding more crumbs as needed.

steps.title: Enrich
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in 30 g butter.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon into a warm bowl, sprinkle with cayenne and parsley, and garnish with a bay leaf and a few cloves not to be eaten, then serve warm.

tips: Keep the milk at the lowest simmer while it infuses; letting it boil can cause it to separate.
Adjust the consistency at the end with a splash more milk if it's too thick, or an extra spoonful of breadcrumbs if it's too thin.
Remove the clove-studded onion and herbs before thickening, as they're only there to flavour the milk.
storage: Best served warm straight away, though it can be covered and gently reheated, loosening with a little milk if it has thickened on standing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
